plan: With a high private value of $48, my goal is to win the auction while minimizing my payment. Other bidders likely have values between $0-$49. A dominant strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, I'll bid strategically close to my value but not exactly at it. A bid around $45 allows room for potential profit if my value is truly high.

With a private value of $38, I want to bid strategically. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid close to, but not exceeding, my true value. Other bidders likely have values between $0-$49. A bid around $35-$39 seems rational - high enough to have a good chance of winning, but not so high that I risk paying more than my value if I win. I'll aim to maximize potential profit by bidding just under my true value.

With a private value of $12, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the auction uses second-price sealed bidding, I want to bid strategically. A pure optimal strategy is to bid my true value ($12), which protects against both overbidding and underbidding. This ensures I win if my value is competitive and prevents paying more than the item is worth to me. With values drawn randomly between $0-$49, a true value bid seems most rational.
